original.reason: The parity argument is false: both a and b may be odd, so it does not establish an even element. The claimed gcd fact is unproved, the transition involving an element 2 is unsupported, and the proof is truncated before establishing 1 or all integers.

judgment.reason: The central lemma is merely asserted: the displayed difference identities do not show that differences or Euclidean remainders are elements of T under the given closure. The simultaneous descent is not defined or justified. Moreover, n↦1−n alone only swaps pairs and cannot generate every integer from 0 and 1.

Its Euclidean-descent lemma is unsupported: having differences in a generated collection does not place them in T. The alleged decreasing quantity and termination conclusion are unspecified. Finally, invariance under n↦1−n does not imply closure under adding or subtracting 1.

The stated descent construction is not supplied and is not implied by closure under x²−y. Its claim that the shifted gcd is preserved through the construction is also unsubstantiated. The final alternating use of n↦1−n cannot yield all integers.

The proof of the central claim only asserts that Euclidean algorithm steps can be simulated; the identities involve subtraction, for which T has no established closure. No precise descent or terminal-pair argument is given. The final assertion that the involution n↦1−n produces all consecutive integers is false.
